title: elif vs Separate if Statements

bugs.explanation: Using two separate `if` statements means both can execute. If `x = 15`, both 'big' and 'medium' are printed. If only one branch should run, use `elif` so the second condition is only checked when the first is false.

title: Nested Conditions
Wrong Indentation in Else

bugs.explanation: `else` must be at the same indentation level as its matching `if`. The `else` here is indented inside the `if` body, which is a `SyntaxError`. Unindent `else:` and the block under it.

title: Ternary Expression
code:

label = 'odd' if n % 2 != 0 else 'even'
print(label)

title: Comparing With None Using ==

bugs.explanation: Use `is None` rather than `== None`. The `==` operator can be overridden by a class's `__eq__` method, giving unexpected results. `is` checks identity and is always correct for `None` checks.

title: All Conditions Checked After Return
Assignment in Condition

bugs.explanation: `=` is assignment, not comparison. Using `=` inside an `if` is a `SyntaxError` in Python (unlike C where it would silently assign). Use `==` to compare, or simply `if not data:` to check for an empty list.

Missing colon After if
code:
x = 10
if x > 5
    print('big')

bugs.explanation: Python `if` statements require a colon `:` at the end of the condition line. Missing it causes `SyntaxError: expected ':'`.

title: Precedence of not

bugs.explanation: `not` has lower precedence than `==` but higher than `or`. The expression parses as `(not (x == 0)) or (x == 1)`, not `not (x == 0 or x == 1)`. Use parentheses to make intent explicit.

Redundant else After Return

bugs.explanation: After `return True`, execution leaves the function — the `else` is redundant. The `else` block runs only when the `if` condition is false anyway. Flatten it to just `return False` after the `if` block.
